about_lede: Elections Archive is a free archive of election results, from each country's first elections to its latest, down to the finest unit the official count reports.
about_holds_body:
The archive covers ten countries and the European Union: the United States, the United Kingdom, Switzerland, Canada, Türkiye, Italy, Germany, France, Ireland, and Brazil. It goes back to 1787 in the United States, 1832 in the United Kingdom, and 1848 in Switzerland, and down to precincts, polling stations, and ballot boxes where the official count goes that deep.

Depth varies by country and year. The [coverage page](/coverage) measures each country against an external count of its elections and lists what is still missing.
about_promises_body:
- **Free, always.** No paid tier, no paywall, and no ads.
- **A source for every number.** Each figure links to the source that published it and to the change that added it. Figures read from scanned books keep the page they came from.
- **Declared, then checked.** Official winners and seats are shown as declared. The archive's own seat calculations sit beside them and never replace them.
- **Open.** The code is free software and the data is free to reuse. See the [license](/license).
- **No tracking.** No analytics, no tracking scripts, and no selling of data. See the [privacy policy](/privacy).
- **For people and agents.** Every page also comes as Markdown and JSON, and the same data is available through an API and an [MCP server](/agents).
about_status_body: The site is a public preview. You can read everything, use the API, and create an account. Contributions open later; the [contribute page](/contribute) explains how they will work and how to help today.
about_maker_body: Elections Archive is made by [Firat Ciftci](https://www.firatciftci.com). The source code is on [GitHub](https://github.com/electarchive/electionsarchive).
about_contact_body: Write to [hello@electionsarchive.com](mailto:hello@electionsarchive.com). To report a wrong number, use the [data error form](https://github.com/electarchive/electionsarchive/issues/new?template=data-error.yml) on GitHub.
about_tribal_body: Results for a tribal nation come only from what that nation's own election body publishes openly, and they are credited to it. News tallies and Bureau of Indian Affairs files are never used in their place. A nation can ask us to withdraw or limit its data at any time, and we will honor the request. Write to [hello@electionsarchive.com](mailto:hello@electionsarchive.com).
license_lede: The data is free to reuse under CC BY 4.0, and the code is free software under the AGPL. Credit the archive and its sources, and you can use the data for anything.
license_data_body: Unless a page says otherwise, the results, places, boundaries, and other data are published under [Creative Commons Attribution 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) (CC BY 4.0). You can copy, share, and adapt them, for commercial use or not, as long as you give credit.
license_sources_body:
Some sources publish under their own licenses, and their data stays under those licenses. Each result set records its source's license, and every page shows it in the source details. For example:

- Some boundary files are under the [Open Database License](https://opendatacommons.org/licenses/odbl/), which asks that adapted versions be shared under the same license.
- European boundaries from Eurostat's GISCO are for non-commercial use, with the credit "© EuroGeographics for the administrative boundaries."
- Historical US county boundaries from the Newberry Library's Atlas of Historical County Boundaries are under CC BY-NC-SA 2.5.
- Some data from the University of Florida Election Lab is under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0.
- Some city ward maps follow each city's own terms.
license_ownership_body:
Election results are public records, published by the authorities that count them. The archive does not claim to own those facts. What it adds, such as the cleaning, matching, and structure, is released under CC BY 4.0 so anyone can build on it.

Party logos and candidate photos belong to their owners and keep their own licenses.
license_contributions_body: When you contribute a correction or new data, you agree to publish it under CC BY 4.0, and the archive credits you by username.
license_cite_body: Cite Elections Archive in one of the formats below, and link to the page you used. When you rely on one source's figures, credit that source too; each page names it.
license_code_body: The source code is licensed under the [GNU Affero General Public License v3.0](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/agpl-3.0.html). If you run a modified version as a public service, you must share your changes under the same license.
contribute_lede: Soon anyone will be able to fix a mistake or add missing results, with a source for every change. Here is how that will work, and how to help today.
contribute_today_body:
- **Report a mistake.** Use the [data error form](https://github.com/electarchive/electionsarchive/issues/new?template=data-error.yml). Link the page and a source that shows the right value.
- **Suggest a source.** Use the [new source form](https://github.com/electarchive/electionsarchive/issues/new?template=new-source.yml) for official results the archive doesn't use yet.
- **Send code.** Open a [pull request](https://github.com/electarchive/electionsarchive/pulls). [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/electarchive/electionsarchive/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) covers the setup and the checks.
- **Report a vulnerability privately**, as [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/electarchive/electionsarchive/blob/main/SECURITY.md) explains.
contribute_how_body:
1. **Sign up** with email, GitHub, or Google, pick a username, and agree to publish your work under CC BY 4.0.
2. **Edit.** Open the page with the mistake, choose Edit, and make the change.
3. **Cite.** Every number, name, date, or outcome you change needs a source: a link, which the archive saves a copy of, or an uploaded document with the page and the spot on it.
4. **Check.** Your proposal becomes a changeset and goes through the same checks as the archive's own data.
5. **Review.** Small, low-risk fixes are reviewed quickly. Changes to winners or seats get a closer look.
6. **Publish.** Once accepted, the change goes live with your name on it. The proposal, its evidence, and the decision stay public.
contribute_agents_body: AI agents will be able to propose changes through the [MCP server](/agents) with an API key. Every key belongs to a person, who is credited for what the agent submits and answers for it. Each proposal records which agent and model made it.
contribute_limits_body: New accounts can make a few proposals a day, and the limit grows as their work is accepted.
architecture_lede: One database holds every result. Everything on the site, from these pages to the API, reads from it, and the only way to write to it is a changeset.
architecture_database_body:
Results, places, boundaries, parties, people, offices, and sources live in one PostgreSQL database with PostGIS. A contest's figures from one source form a result set, and each result set records its source, its license, and the changeset that wrote it.

Official winners and seats are stored as declared. A seat engine, tested against real elections, recomputes them for comparison and never overwrites them.
architecture_in_body:
1. **Fetch.** A pipeline downloads the official file, book, or feed and keeps a checksummed copy of the original.
2. **Parse.** It reads the file into tables. Figures read from scanned books keep the page and the box on that page they came from.
3. **Emit.** It writes a changeset: one package of new and changed records.
4. **Check.** The changeset is staged, and checks match its places, parties, and people and test that its totals add up.
5. **Publish.** The changeset is applied, and every record it wrote points back to it.

Proposals from people and agents will take the same path, with review in place of a pipeline.
architecture_out_body:
- **The website**, rendered on the server, so pages work without JavaScript.
- **Markdown and JSON** versions of every page: add .md or .json to the address.
- **A REST API**, described by [OpenAPI](/api/v1/openapi.json).
- **An MCP server** for AI agents, described on the [agents page](/agents).
- **Embeds** of maps and tables for other sites.
- **Bulk downloads** are planned.
architecture_maps_body: Boundaries are stored with every election that used them and served as vector tiles from PMTiles files. The browser draws them with MapLibre and colors each shape from the results.
architecture_live_body: On election nights, the site polls official feeds and stores each update as a preliminary snapshot, so the count can be replayed later. The [election-night model](/live/methodology) explains the estimates.
architecture_search_body: Search runs inside PostgreSQL, with trigram and full-text matching that ignores accents.
architecture_hosting_body: The site runs on one server behind Cloudflare, which caches pages for up to five minutes.
architecture_code_body: The code is on [GitHub](https://github.com/electarchive/electionsarchive). The [architecture guide](https://github.com/electarchive/electionsarchive/blob/main/docs/architecture.md), the [data model](https://github.com/electarchive/electionsarchive/blob/main/docs/data-model.md), and the [pipeline guide](https://github.com/electarchive/electionsarchive/blob/main/docs/pipelines.md) go deeper.
privacy_lede: The archive collects as little about you as it can. There are no ads, no analytics, and no tracking scripts, and no data is sold.
privacy_reading_body:
You don't need an account to read the archive or use the API. The site sets no cookies unless you sign in or choose a language.

Your browser stores a few settings on your device, such as your theme, your recent searches, and your election-night layout. They are never sent to the server.
privacy_network_body:
All traffic passes through Cloudflare, which caches pages and protects the site from attacks. Cloudflare processes your IP address and request details under its [privacy policy](https://www.cloudflare.com/privacypolicy/).

To limit abuse, the server counts requests per IP address. These counts expire on their own, within a day at most, and are used for nothing else.
privacy_accounts_body:
If you create an account, the archive stores your email address, your username, and anything you add to your profile, such as a display name and bio. Your username, display name, and bio are public. A session cookie keeps you signed in.

If you sign in with GitHub or Google, that service shares your name and email address with the archive. Sign-in and verification emails are sent through [Cloudflare](https://www.cloudflare.com/privacypolicy/).
privacy_contributions_body: When contributions open, your proposals, the evidence you attach, and the decisions on them will be public and credited to your username.
privacy_newsletter_body: If you subscribe to updates, [Buttondown](https://buttondown.com/legal/privacy) stores your email address and sends the emails. Every email has a link to unsubscribe.
privacy_people_body: Candidate records hold only what election authorities publish, such as names, parties, and results, plus links to Wikidata. The archive does not publish home addresses or contact details. To ask for a correction, write to [hello@electionsarchive.com](mailto:hello@electionsarchive.com).
privacy_rights_body: To delete your account or get a copy of your data, write to [hello@electionsarchive.com](mailto:hello@electionsarchive.com). If this policy changes, the date at the top of this page changes with it.
terms_lede: These terms cover your use of electionsarchive.com, its API, and its MCP server. They are short and written in plain language.
terms_use_body: You may read, search, download, and reuse the archive for any lawful purpose, under the terms of its [licenses](/license).
terms_api_body: The API and the MCP server are free and need no key for reading. Keep requests to a reasonable rate, and don't try to get around the rate limits. If you need large amounts of data, write to [hello@electionsarchive.com](mailto:hello@electionsarchive.com) before crawling.
terms_accuracy_body:
The archive links every number to its source and works to get each one right, but it can contain errors. The official declaration of the election authority is the final word. Estimates shown on election nights are projections from partial counts, not results.

The archive is provided as is, without warranty of any kind.
terms_accounts_body: Keep your sign-in details safe. You are responsible for what is done with your account and your API keys, including by agents you run. Accounts that abuse the site may be suspended.
terms_contributions_body: Only submit what you have the right to share, cite real sources, and never submit data you know is false. Contributions are published under CC BY 4.0.
terms_liability_body: To the extent the law allows, Elections Archive and its maker are not liable for any loss that comes from using the site or its data.
terms_changes_body: These terms may change. When they do, the date at the top of this page changes with them. Send questions to [hello@electionsarchive.com](mailto:hello@electionsarchive.com).

party_strength_missing: No map of the party's vote available for this election.
scrubber_lede: Drag the years or press play to see maps, the elected chamber, and the resulting government.
map_rebuilding: This map is being rebuilt. Check back in a few minutes.
search_error: Search didn’t answer. Check your connection and try again.
search_short: Keep typing to search the archive.
map_pick_touch: Tap a place to see its results.
provenance_scan: Digitized from page {page} of {title}. The highlighted box marks the number.
provenance_crop_alt: Scan of page {page} with the number highlighted
provenance_parts: This total is the sum of figures from {count} smaller places, each digitized from a printed page. The first is shown.
method_share: Share is the option's votes divided by all valid votes in the same place.
method_seats: Seats are recorded exactly as declared by the authority. The archive does not recalculate them.
method_swing: Swing is the change in the gap between the top two options from one election to the next, in percentage points.
method_stage: When multiple counts exist, the page shows the most final: certified, official, or preliminary.
provenance_share_note: Valid votes leave out blank and spoiled ballots.
winners_lede: Shows winners of all {count} races, grouped by {noun}, and the party with the most wins in each.
winners_led_note: The sources declare no winner in {count} of these races, so the candidate with the most votes is shown and marked Led.
sweep_verdict_both: {party} won the most votes and the most {nouns}
sweep_verdict_split: {party} won the most votes, {rival} the most {nouns}
sweep_summary: {party} won {won} of {total} {nouns} and {share} of the vote.
sweep_summary_since: {party} won {won} of {total} {nouns} and {share} of the vote, against {before} {nouns} and {earlier} in {year}.
sweep_measure_mixed: Vote shares add metropolitan mayor votes in {mayors} {nouns} to provincial council votes in the other {councils}, the usual way to compare parties nationally.
sweep_measure_councils: Vote shares count provincial council votes in all {count} {nouns}, the usual way to compare parties nationally.
sweep_measure_mayors: Vote shares count metropolitan mayor votes in all {count} {nouns}.
versus_verdict_places: {a} and {b} picked the same winner in {same} of {total} contests ({share}).
versus_tape_drift: Average gap from the entire race
versus_ledger_places_key: Each square is one contest in one year. The upper-left half is {a} and the lower-right half is {b}, colored by the winner and shaded by the margin. Hover or use the arrow keys to read a square, then click it again or press Enter to open the contest.
versus_ledger_parties_key: Each square is one contest in one year. The upper-left half is {a} and the lower-right half is {b}, shaded by vote share. An outlined half means the party did not run. Hover or use the arrow keys to read a square, then click it again or press Enter to open the contest.
versus_duel_key: The winning margin in each place, with {first} above the center line and {second} below it. The shading between the lines shows which party the gap between {a} and {b} favors, and the bars underneath show its size.
versus_gap_help: The difference between {a} and {b}, in percentage points. The marker shows which side it favors.
versus_helix_key: {a} runs above the axis and {b} below it. Each mark is a race, placed by vote share and sized by votes. Filled marks are wins and faded marks are primaries. Bars on the axis show time in office, and lines join the races where they faced each other.
versus_races_key: Shaded rows are races they both ran in. A filled marker means a win.
versus_verdict_people: Head to head on the same ballot: {a} {one}, {b} {two}.
versus_verdict_people_none: {a} and {b} never appeared on the same ballot.
versus_verdict_parties: {a} finished ahead of {b} in {one} of the {total} contests where both ran.
coverage_upcoming_def: Still to vote, and the archive already holds everything but the results: the office or seat, the district, the voting system, and every candidate with their party, or for a ballot measure, its answers and official wording. These count as covered until election day. From the next day they need results.
coverage_reason_pending_def: Still to vote. The archive holds the race but lacks something it needs before election day: candidates, their parties, the voting system, or for a ballot measure, its answers or official wording.
coverage_upcoming_note: Races that haven't voted yet count as covered once the archive holds their candidates, or a measure's answers and wording, in full. The day after the vote, they need results like any other race.

coverage_lede: This shows how much of the US election record the archive holds, measured against every contest it should hold. The counts come straight from the database.
coverage_goal_turnout_note: Before 1948, many states kept no statewide count of registered voters, so earlier elections are not counted yet. North Dakota has had no voter registration since 1951, so its elections need only ballots cast.
coverage_reason_complete_turnout_def: The archive has both the number of registered voters and the number of ballots cast or voters checked in.
coverage_reason_turnout_partial_def: The archive has registered voters or ballots cast, but not both.
coverage_reason_turnout_coarse_def: The archive has only the Census Bureau's survey estimate of registration and voting, not the official counts.
coverage_reason_turnout_absent_def: Election days with no turnout figures in the archive yet.
coverage_goal_local_note: Local governments come from the 2022 Census of Governments. Special districts are counted only if their boards are elected. Districts with appointed boards, as the Census Bureau's Individual State Descriptions report them, are left out. A government is due to vote in the years its election history shows. If the archive has no election history for a government, the state's local election calendar for that type of government applies, as set by state election law. Where the law could not be confirmed, the cycle is estimated.
coverage_progress_local_population: {percent} of local elections, weighted by population
coverage_local_two_measures: A local election here means one government voting in one year: a city that elects its council every two years counts once for each of those years. Each local ballot measure counts as one. The population share weights each government by its population, so a city of a million people counts a thousand times as much as a town of a thousand. The population share is higher because the governments the archive holds are mostly large ones.
coverage_local_weights: Each government counts by its population. Counties, cities, and townships use the Census Bureau's estimates. School districts use the Bureau's school district population estimates.
coverage_local_estimated: {percent} of that weight is estimated. The Census Bureau publishes no population for special districts, and none for some school districts. Those districts take the population of their city or county, split evenly among the districts of the same kind that share it. For example, 20 special districts in a county of 100,000 people count 5,000 people each.
coverage_tip_held_def: Counts every contest the archive holds in any form. Only those not in the archive yet are left out.
coverage_tip_complete_def: Counts only contests with complete results at this level. Partial results, known gaps, and blocked contests are left out.
coverage_reason_complete_county_def: The archive has results by county, town, or precinct. A district that lies entirely within one county also counts as a county result, since its total is that county's result.
coverage_reason_complete_history_def: The archive has the contest's results by county, town, or precinct.
coverage_reason_complete_district_def: The archive has the contest's vote counts for the whole district.
coverage_reason_complete_precinct_def: The archive has results by precinct. Primaries canceled because no one ran against the nominee are included.
coverage_reason_complete_local_def: The archive holds at least one of the government's contests that year.
coverage_reason_complete_shapes_def: The contest's district has a shape for the election date, as does every county, town, or Alaska house district in its results. Statewide contests use the state's shape.
coverage_reason_major_def: The archive has precinct results, but they leave out at least one candidate who won 0.5% or more of the vote, usually because the source lists only the Democratic and Republican candidates. These results don't count toward the goal until an official or complete precinct source replaces them.
coverage_reason_coarse_def: The archive has results by county or town, but not yet by precinct.
coverage_reason_partial_def: The archive has county or precinct results that cover fewer than 90% of the state's counties or add up to less than the official total.
coverage_reason_totals_def: The archive has the statewide or district total, but no results by county.
coverage_reason_bare_def: The archive lists the contest and its candidates, but it has no vote counts. Most of these are unopposed races.
coverage_reason_absent_def: Contests the election calendar says took place that the archive doesn't have yet.
coverage_reason_absent_local_def: Years a government was due to hold an election that the archive has none of its contests for.
coverage_reason_units_def: The district has a shape, but at least one county, town, or Alaska house district in the results has no shape for the election date.
coverage_reason_unshaped_def: The archive has this district, but no map of its lines as they were on the election date.
coverage_unshaped_span: Most of these are elections in {years}, whose district maps the archive doesn't hold yet.
coverage_unshaped_span_redraw: Most of these are elections in {years}, which still used the district lines drawn in the 1990s.
coverage_reason_precinct_shaped_def: The precinct has a map shape for the election date.
coverage_reason_precinct_unshaped_def: The archive has the precinct's results but no map shape for it.
coverage_reason_undrawn_def: The contest has no district, or its district has never had a shape, such as New Hampshire's floterial seats.
coverage_where_hint: Open a state to see its offices, then an office to see its years.
coverage_column_note: The Missing column counts the contests or races that don't meet this level of detail, election days for turnout, or local elections (one government voting in one year) for local governments. The bar colors match the legend above.
coverage_icpsr_def: Complete, but the only county results come from ICPSR's historical files or from Algara and Amlani's returns compiled from them. Official returns will replace them.
coverage_published_def: Complete, because no official body published precinct results for these races. The archive holds the county or town results that were published. For each state and year, it also keeps the proof, such as a statute or the state's canvass format.
coverage_stale: Rebuilt before the latest denominators and counting rules, so some numbers here may be out of date until the next rebuild.
coverage_gov_more: {count} smaller governments are not listed. This page shows the 500 largest.
coverage_gov_lede: Every local government of this kind in this state in the 2022 Census of Governments, largest first. Each row shows the latest year the archive holds its results, its next election, the law or charter that sets its election cycle, and where its results are published. The readiness count on the coverage page is smaller: it counts only governments with a November 3 election, so a state's list here can be longer.
coverage_gov_year_lede: Only governments due to vote in {year}. Those the archive is missing come first.
coverage_gov_twin_hint: To list one state's governments of one kind, add `?state=` and `&level=` to this page's address, as in `?state=CA&level=municipality`. Each row gives the government's next election, the law that sets its cycle, and where its results are published. The kinds are {levels}. Add `&year=` to list only the governments due to vote that year.
coverage_country_lede: This shows how much of the election record the archive holds, measured against official counts of the elections that took place. Counts come directly from the database.
coverage_country_facts: The archive holds {elections} elections here, from {first} to {last}.
coverage_country_none: No official count has been compiled for this goal yet, so there is no figure.
coverage_country_def_national: The archive has the constituency's votes, or the whole contest's votes for a presidential election or a by-election, and they add up to at least 98% of the declared total. Where no declared total is stored, every unit of the race must be present. Unopposed returns count too.
coverage_country_def_fine: The archive has results finer than the constituency, such as municipalities or polling districts, and they add up to at least 98% of the constituency's declared total.
coverage_country_def_shapes: The constituency has a map shape valid on election day.
coverage_country_def_subnational: The archive has the constituency's votes, and they add up to at least 98% of the declared total. Where no declared total is stored, every unit of the race must be present. Unopposed returns count too.
coverage_country_def_local: The archive has the votes for that council, municipality, or local electoral area, and they add up to at least 98% of the declared total. Where no declared total is stored, every unit must be present.
coverage_country_def_referendums: The archive has the referendum's results by region or finer, and they add up to at least 98% of the declared total. Where no declared total is stored, every region must be present.
coverage_country_def_ep: The archive has the constituency's votes, and they add up to at least 98% of the declared total. Where no declared total is stored, every unit must be present.
coverage_canvass: Precinct results kept despite a wrong canvass
coverage_canvass_def: In these races the official canvass is wrong, so the archive counts the precinct results as complete without matching them to it. The note for each one explains why.
coverage_ready_title: Ready for the November 3, 2026, general election
coverage_ready_lede: This counts how many of the races on the November 3 ballot the archive already holds with their candidates. The total comes from official lists of what is up for election. State legislatures and the U.S. House count seats, ballot measures count measures, statewide courts count states, and county, city, and school board offices count local governments. Local courts count the races the archive holds, since no official list gives their number.
coverage_ready_complete_def: The race has more candidates than seats, or exactly as many when it's uncontested on an official state list. A ballot measure is ready once both answers are in.
coverage_ready_partial_def: The race is in the archive, but only some of its candidates are.
coverage_ready_bare_def: The race is in the archive, but none of its candidates are.
coverage_ready_absent_def: The official list includes the race, but the archive doesn't have it yet.
coverage_ready_of_states: {held} of {total} states in the archive, {ready} ready
coverage_ready_of_governments: {held} of {total} governments in the archive, {ready} ready
coverage_ready_of_held: {held} of {total} races in the archive, {ready} ready
coverage_ready_of_measures: {held} of {total} measures in the archive, {ready} ready
coverage_ready_schedule: Other statewide offices are counted from each office's term length and its past elections, then checked against each Secretary of State's candidate list.
coverage_reason_known_gap_def: Every source the archive has tried is exhausted. Each gap below gives the reason, the sources tried, and the date checked.
coverage_reason_blocked_def: A source holds these results, but the archive can't reach it yet: the site blocks scripts, the record exists only in print, or a manual download is pending.
coverage_reason_inapplicable_def: Left out of the count because this grain doesn't exist for these races, as when votes are declared only for the constituency as a whole.
polity_known_lede: What the archive can't fill yet, and why. Data that nobody has looked for yet isn't listed here; the coverage page counts it as missing.
coverage_country_reason_partial_def: The archive has votes for the race, but they add up to less than 98% of the declared total, or some of the race's units are missing.
coverage_country_reason_coarse_def: The archive has the constituency's votes, but nothing finer yet.
coverage_country_reason_totals_def: The archive has only totals, not results for each constituency or area.
coverage_country_reason_bare_def: The archive lists the contest and its candidates, but it has no vote counts.
coverage_country_reason_absent_def: The official count lists it, but the archive doesn't have it yet.
coverage_country_reason_unshaped_def: The constituency has a map shape, but not one valid on election day.
coverage_country_reason_undrawn_def: The constituency has no map shape yet, or the contest isn't in the archive.
coverage_ledger_held: Contests in the archive from these years: {count}
coverage_ledger_unlisted: The archive also holds contests from years the official count doesn't list: {years}.
coverage_where_hint_country: Open a region to see its kinds of election, then one of those to see its years.
coverage_where_hint_flat: Open a kind of election to see its years.
coverage_sources_hint: The official counts each goal is measured against.
coverage_classes_hint: Every kind of election held at each tier of government, including those the archive does not hold yet. A kind counts as held once the archive has any of its results.
coverage_classes_legend: Queued kinds of election are being loaded; open ones are not yet planned.
coverage_classes_overview_hint: Every kind of election each country holds, by tier of government. Countries whose kinds of election are not listed yet are left out.
coverage_overview_lede: How much of each country's election record the archive holds, measured against official counts of the elections that took place. Every figure comes straight from the database.
coverage_overview_totals: The archive holds {elections} elections and {contests} contests, from {first} to {last}.
coverage_overview_explain_count: Each country's official list comes from the statutes, electoral commissions, and statistical offices cited on its page. The archive's own records never decide what belongs on it.
coverage_overview_explain_gaps: Where no official list exists for a kind of election or a span of years, the country's page says so instead of guessing.
coverage_glance_hint_country: Each cell shows the share of races that meet that level of detail. A race is one constituency at one election, or the whole contest when a presidential election, by-election, or referendum is counted nationwide. A dash means that detail isn't measured for these elections.
coverage_glance_hint_us: Each cell shows the share of contests that meet that level of detail, primaries and runoffs included. The precinct shapes row counts precincts instead, and its target starts in 2016; earlier shapes are a bonus. A dash means that detail isn't measured for these contests.
coverage_glance_none_hint: No count yet means no official count of these elections has been found to measure against, so there is no figure.
coverage_note_history_1824: Federal and statewide contests before 1824 aren't counted yet.
coverage_note_shapes: Precinct shapes are counted separately, under Precinct shapes.
coverage_note_precinct_shapes: Public precinct shapes start in 2016 with the Voting and Election Science Team's files, so the target starts there too. The count is deduplicated: sources sometimes give one precinct different codes, so until they share one, precincts are matched by county and precinct number.
coverage_note_precinct_shapes_bonus: Few public precinct shapes exist before 2016, so the ones the archive has are a bonus, and precincts without one aren't counted as missing. The Census Bureau's 2010 voting districts could add shapes for 2008–2012.
coverage_turnout: Turnout is recorded for {count} of the {held} contests the archive holds.
coverage_rebuilding: Coverage is being recalculated. These figures will change when it finishes.
coverage_ledger_strip: {label}: official count for {counted}; no official count yet for {uncounted}
coverage_tier_def_federal: President, U.S. Senate, and U.S. House contests, primaries and runoffs included.
coverage_tier_def_statewide: Governor, other statewide offices, and statewide courts, primaries and runoffs included. Each kind is listed separately below.
coverage_tier_def_legislative: State senate and state house contests, primaries and runoffs included. Before 2000, most states printed only district totals for their legislatures, so those years are measured by district total, not by county.
coverage_tier_def_local_us: Every county, city, township, school district, and special district that elects officials, from the 2022 Census of Governments, for each year it was due to hold an election since 2000.
coverage_tier_def_precinct_shapes: Every precinct with results from 2000, counted once per state and year however many contests it reported, and whether the archive has its map shape for that year. The target starts in 2016.
coverage_tier_def_turnout: Registered voters and ballots cast for every statewide election day: general elections from 1948, and primaries, runoffs, and statewide referendums from 2000. Turnout counts when the archive has both figures.
coverage_tier_def_national: Elections to the national parliament and, where there is one, the presidency, by-elections included.
coverage_tier_def_subnational: Elections to regional, state, or devolved legislatures and governorships.
coverage_tier_def_referendums: Nationwide referendums, measured by results for each region.
coverage_tier_def_referendums_us: Statewide ballot measures, counted against the National Conference of State Legislatures' Statewide Ballot Measures Database, which lists the measures each state has voted on since 1902. Where the archive holds more measures than NCSL lists for a state and year, such as Washington's advisory votes, the archive's count is used.
coverage_tier_def_ep: European Parliament elections, measured by results for each constituency.
coverage_overview_column_tiers: Share of races the archive holds with results, one race per constituency at each election
coverage_overview_done_body: A kind of election is done when the archive has the votes for every constituency in every election on an official list. Each country's page also tracks results below the constituency and map shapes. US pages go further: they separate races before 2000 from races since 2000, add results by county and by precinct, and add precinct shapes, with precinct figures shown for 2000–2015 and for 2016 onward.
coverage_overview_note: Every cell uses the same measure: the share of races that the archive holds results for at the race's own level. That level is the constituency or district, or the whole state or country for a statewide or national race. Outside the US, a race counts only when its votes reach 98% of the declared total. For US local governments, a cell counts the local elections (one government voting in one year) with any results. Results by county, precinct, or other finer units are on each country's page.
map_no_results: No results available for this contest
map_missing_places: The archive doesn't have {noun} boundaries, so these results can't be drawn on a map. The table below lists them by {noun}.
map_missing_drawn: Boundaries exist for these results, but they couldn't be drawn on a map.
map_missing_whole: These results are a single total for the whole contest, with no breakdown by place that could be shown on a map.
results_all_write_ins: No one was on the ballot. Every vote here was written in.
map_pending: Results not in the archive yet
places_pending: Results not in the archive yet: {names}.
map_unmatched_redrawn_line: Redrawn since {year}. It shares {percent} of its ground with the current version and isn't compared.
map_unmatched_missing_line: No result recorded for this area in {year}, so it isn't compared.
map_estimated_line: Estimated: the {year} result is built from the {year} areas that overlap this one.
places_others_note: The county source groups {name} with minor candidates; they appear as one group on this map.
seats_up: {count} of {total} seats were up for election. Faded dots represent seats not up.
map_turnout_key: Share of registered voters who cast a ballot
control_none: No overall control: no party won a majority of the {total} seats
control_derived: Worked out from the seats won, since the whole council was up for election.
control_rolled: Worked out from the seats won at this election and the two before it, or back to the last election where every seat was up. By-elections and changes of party aren't counted.
councils_lede: {count} councils held elections. Control is worked out from the seats won: at this election where the whole council was up, and over the last three elections where a third of the council is elected each year. By-elections and changes of party aren't counted.
turnout_partial: Based on {reporting} of {of} jurisdictions reporting both registered voters and ballots cast.
map_turnout_change_key: Turnout change since the compared election
council_members_lede: Who holds each seat, as of the latest election for it.
council_map_title: What happened to each seat in the {election}
council_changes_lede: Each election's seats: members returned, open seats, and incumbents who lost.
council_sizes_lede: Counted from the seats filled at each election, starting in {year}, the first year the archive covers a full term.
council_tenures_note: The archive doesn't hold appointments, resignations, or deaths for this council yet, so each member's time runs from one election to the next.
explain_access: {beaten} won more votes but fewer seats, because only lists that won a whole quota in at least one constituency shared the seats left over after whole quotas.
explain_access_votes: {beaten} won more votes but fewer seats, because only lists that won a whole quota in at least one constituency and at least {votes} votes nationwide shared the seats left over after whole quotas.
explain_remainder: {who} won this seat from the national remainder, a pool that fills the seats that districts leave after whole quotas by each party's leftover votes nationwide, so a list can win one here with few votes.
explain_compensation: {who} won list seats here with fewer votes than parties that took constituency seats, because list seats make up for the constituency results: each party's list votes are divided by one more than the seats it already holds in the region.
explain_threshold: {beaten} won more votes here but fewer seats, because only parties with at least {percent}% of the vote nationwide take seats.
explain_pooling: {who} won a seat with fewer votes than some lists outside its alliance, because seats are shared out among alliances first and then within each one.
explain_bonus: {who} won a seat with fewer votes than some other lists, because the winning list or coalition receives bonus seats on top of its share.
explain_independent: {person} won {list}'s seat as an independent on its list.
explain_independent_joined: {person} won {list}'s seat as an independent on its list and joined the party on {date}.
live_meta_description: Results from {place}'s election night on {date}, update by update, from the official count.
live_replay_note: A replay of the night, built from the updates the Board of Elections posted and the Internet Archive captured. The captures are sparse, so some races show only their last update.
live_of_certified: {share} of the final certified count ({count} votes)
live_scanners_note: This is the share of the Board's scanners that had sent results. Early votes are counted first, so early in the night the vote count runs ahead of this share.
live_scanners_none: The Board hadn't published scanner shares by this time.
live_after_night: The certified count added {count} votes ({share} of the total) after the last update on election night.
live_council_note: {captured} of {total} districts had a captured update by this time.
live_council_note_final: {captured} of {total} districts had an update captured on election night. Every district shows its certified count.
live_waiting_night: No results yet. Counts appear here as the officials publish them, and this page checks for new ones every 30 seconds.
live_rehearsal_note: A synthetic night for testing this page. It scales each county's certified result along a made-up reporting order, so these are not real election-night counts.
live_replay_note_state: A replay of the night, built from the updates the state's results site posted.
live_reporting_note: The share of precincts or counties that had sent results, as the results site counts them. Early and mail votes often arrive first, so the vote count can run ahead of this share.
live_district_note_final: {counted} of {total} districts reported on election night. Every district shows its certified count.
live_stale: No new results since {time}. The official site may have paused its count; this page keeps checking every 30 seconds.
live_offline: Can't reach the archive right now, so these are the last results this page loaded. It tries again every 30 seconds.
live_map_waiting: No district results by this time
live_sentence_leads: {name} leads by {margin} points with {counted} votes counted.
live_sentence_won: {name} was elected with {share} of the vote in the certified count.
live_no_update: No update captured by this time
live_twin_summary: Results as {publisher} posted them through election night, then the certified count. To see another moment, add ?at= with one of the update times below, or ?at=final for the certified count.
live_landing_note: Each state's count appears here as its official results site publishes it. This page checks for new results every minute. Open a state to follow its races.
live_landing_twin: Every state's live results, as its official site publishes them. Each state's link opens its races and shows every update; add .md or .json to it for the plain-text or data version.
live_twin_note: Counts as each state's official results site posts them; the archive checks every 30 seconds. To see an earlier moment, add ?at= with one of the update times below, or ?at=final for the certified count. The estimates come from this archive's model, not from any official call.
live_twin_estimate: Estimate: {name} has a {chance} chance of winning, with a final margin between {low} and {high} points and about {share} of the expected vote counted.
live_twin_too_early: Estimate: too few votes are in to estimate the result.
live_twin_no_estimate: Estimate: none, because this race has no earlier result to compare with.
live_twin_ranked: Estimate: no chance of winning or final margin, because no one has more than half of first choices and the race goes to the ranked-choice count. About {share} of the expected vote is counted.
live_twin_settled: Estimate: {name} won in the certified count.

method_lede: On election night, the model estimates where each race will end up before every vote is counted. This page explains how the model works, how it was tested, and where it can go wrong.
method_hero_caption: Pennsylvania's 2020 presidential race, replayed from county counts as The New York Times reported them on election night and in the days after, saved by the Internet Archive. The archive saved no copies between 3% and 66% of the vote counted. The dotted line is the margin among the votes counted so far. The shaded band is the model's 80% range for the final margin, and the solid line is its middle.
method_hero_miss: With two-thirds of the vote counted, Trump led by 15 points, and the model gave Biden an 11% chance. From 77% counted, the model's range held Biden's final margin of 1.2 points, and by 84% the model leaned toward Biden. From 96% counted, though, its estimate had Biden winning by 2 to 3 points, and its range missed the final margin: the last ballots still favored Biden, but by less than the mail ballots counted before them.
method_how_body: Every time new votes come in, the model takes each county's latest count and asks two questions: how many votes will this county cast in all, and how will the votes still to come split? It answers both from the counties that have reported, compared with how the same counties voted last time. Then it simulates the rest of the count 500 times.
method_step_baseline_title: Start from the last comparable race
method_step_baseline: Each county's baseline is its result in the last race for the same seat, or in the last presidential race when that race was one-sided or missing. Expected turnout comes from the same past races.
method_step_turnout: The model works out how many votes each county will cast and whether its count is finished.
method_step_swing: Counties that have reported show how far the vote has moved from the baseline. The model fits that movement and applies it to the votes still out.
method_step_simulate_title: Simulate the rest of the count
method_step_simulate: Each of 500 simulations draws a different turnout, swing, and late-count shift, then adds up every county.
method_step_report_title: Report a range and a chance
method_step_report: The middle 80% of the simulations gives the range. Each candidate's chance is the average, across all simulations, of how likely that candidate is to finish ahead.
method_turnout_body: Early in the night, most of the uncertainty is about how many votes are left, not how they lean. A county that has counted 80,000 votes might be finished, or it might still have 40,000 mail ballots to count. The model treats each reporting county as one of two cases: finished, with a final total just above its current count, or still counting, with a final total somewhere above its count and most likely near its expected turnout.
method_turnout_body_more: Which case is more likely depends on three things the model learns from all reporting counties at once: how turnout compares with expectations across the state, how closely counties follow that statewide level, and what share of counties have finished. A county is more likely to be done if its count has not changed for 15 minutes, or for twice its usual time between updates if that is longer. In presidential years, the model starts by expecting turnout a few percent above the last presidential race, until the counts show otherwise. Counties with no votes yet are expected to cast their usual turnout, adjusted by the statewide turnout level seen so far.
method_turnout_caption: A county expected to cast 100,000 votes has counted 80,000. The bar is the chance its count is finished. The curve spreads the chance it is still counting across possible final totals.
method_margin_title: How the remaining votes will split
method_margin_body: For each county, the model compares the margin counted so far with the baseline. Across the reporting counties, it fits five effects:
method_margin_uniform: A uniform swing toward one party across the state.
method_margin_stronghold: A stronghold effect, for when the swing is larger in places one party already dominates.
method_margin_size: A county-size effect, for when big and small counties move differently.
method_margin_traits: A demographic effect: counties with more college graduates, or more white, Black, or Hispanic residents, move differently from the rest, and so do counties whose white, Black, or Hispanic share has grown or shrunk since 2016, compared with counties that changed less. The county figures come from the Census Bureau.
method_margin_order: A count-order effect, for when the votes counted later in a county lean differently from the votes counted first. The model measures this from how each county's margin changed between its earlier and later counts. Where a state reports early, mail, and election-day votes separately, each kind gets its own effect, because the order in which they are counted can lean in different directions. Where a county reports a single total, the model expects the effect to fade quickly as the county nears its expected total, because that expected total is itself an estimate. When the counties' own counts show the difference holding until the end, as when a large batch of mail ballots is counted last, the model instead shrinks the effect only in proportion to the share of votes still out.
method_margin_body_more: Each county's projected margin blends its own count with that fitted prediction, and the more of a county's vote is in, the more weight its own count gets. Each effect starts near zero and grows only as the counted votes support it.
method_order_body: Ballots counted late in the night, or after it, often lean differently from the ones counted first. Mail ballots, provisional ballots, and ballots from large cities can all come in late. Three parts of the model cover this.
method_order_shift: A shared late-count shift moves all the uncounted votes in a race together in each simulation, so the model never assumes that errors in different counties cancel out.
method_order_swing: The model also watches each county's count for swings between early and late votes. As a county reports more votes, the model compares the margin among its newer votes with the margin among its earlier ones. When those swings are larger than ordinary differences between batches, the model widens the range for the votes still out, in proportion to how many are left. When the swings are small, it leaves the range alone.
method_order_tail: In states that keep counting for days or weeks, the model expects more votes after election night, and those votes have a lean of their own. On election night, those late votes count toward each county's projected total instead of being added on top of it, so the model adds only what the county projections leave out. From the second day on, it adds fewer each day, because many of those late votes are already in the count. If the count already runs well past the turnout the county projections predict, the model takes that as a sign that the late votes are already counted and expects fewer of them. The chart shows how many votes each state typically adds for every 100 counted on the night. Nevada has mailed a ballot to every active voter since its June 2020 primary, so its share applies only from then on; earlier Nevada elections use the single share the chart shows for all states not listed.
method_order_after: After election night, the model stops treating counties as finished just because every precinct has reported. Late batches of absentee, affidavit, and provisional ballots can keep arriving for a week or more, and their exact number is often not published. So once the count slows down, the model estimates how many votes are left from the number that came in over the past two days, with a wide range. During the first day after election night, before that estimate starts, a county's projected total is also kept near what the county could add at the pace it has counted since election night, and the model holds to that limit more firmly as the day goes on. It also learns how those late votes lean: it compares each county's votes counted since election night with its margin on the night, pools those differences across counties, and applies that lean to the votes still out. Counties with few late votes are pulled toward the statewide pattern, and the range stays wide when the late batches disagree with each other or when there are few of them. For a county that is still adding votes, the model also looks at the margin among the votes it added over the past day. If the projection has the votes still out leaning further in the same direction as those recent votes did, the model sets their margin to the recent margin. Otherwise, once a full day has passed since the end of election night, it moves their margin halfway toward the recent margin. It waits that day because until then, the past day's votes can still include ballots counted on the night. Nevada counts many mail ballots in the days after the election, and in recent elections those ballots have leaned about 10 points further toward Democrats than each county's earlier count. So in Nevada races, the model projects that the votes still out will lean that way, give or take about 4 points. It starts doing so once the count has paused for four hours after its largest batch of votes, so that the election-day count is in first, and it stops when the late count begins.
method_order_chart: Votes added after election night, for every 100 counted on the night
method_ranges_body: Each simulation ends with a final margin. The range on a race page runs from the 10th to the 90th percentile of the simulations, so the final margin should land inside it about 80% of the time. For the chance of winning, each simulation works out how likely each candidate is to finish ahead given that simulation's turnout and swing, and the page shows the average across all 500. That is steadier than counting how many simulations each candidate wins.
method_ranges_status: A race page shows no favorite until a tenth of the expected vote is counted. Until then, it shows the count and says it is too early to estimate. Once a race is certified, the page shows the certified result.
method_ranges_caption: The 500 simulations behind the replay above, with two-thirds of the vote counted. Each dot is one simulation's final margin.
method_testing_body: The tests replayed {races} races for president (by state), Senate, and governor from 2012 to 2024. Each replay uses the counties' final results, revealed in a simulated order. Each county's votes are split into election-day, early in-person, and mail ballots, with mail ballots leaning further from election-day votes in years like 2020, when mail voting split sharply by party. Some replays count early votes first, some count election-day votes first, and some mix the two. Each replay stopped at 18 points between 3% and 95% of the vote counted, and every estimate the model made there was scored against the final result.
method_testing_summary: Across all simulated checkpoints, the model's Brier score is {brier}, and its middle estimate is {error} points from the final margin on average.
method_testing_real: The model was also tested on {races} races from real election nights, replayed from county counts at the moments they were reported: the 2020 presidential count in Florida, Georgia, North Carolina, and Pennsylvania, and {later} Senate and governor races from 2022. Those counts come from The New York Times results pages, as saved by the Internet Archive.
method_testing_real_result: Real nights were harder. On them, the model's 80% range held the final margin {cover} of the time, and its range for turnout held the final total only {turnout} of the time.
method_testing_repo: The full write-up, the model's estimates at every checkpoint, and the scoring code are on GitHub.

method_limit_pause: Long pauses. A big county that stops counting with many ballots left can look finished, and the model then underestimates how many votes are still out.

indices_effective_meaning: How many equal-sized parties would split the votes or seats the same way. Two big parties and a few small ones count as a little over two.
indices_effective_range: About 2 in two-party systems, 3 to 5 in most multiparty democracies, and above 6 in very fragmented ones.
indices_fragmentation_meaning: The chance that two voters, or two members, picked at random belong to different parties.
indices_fragmentation_range: From 0 when one party has everything to near 1 when many small parties share it. Most parliaments fall between 0.5 and 0.85.
indices_gallagher_meaning: How far each party's share of seats strays from its share of votes. Big gaps count for more than small ones.
indices_gallagher_range: Under 3 in most proportional systems, 5 to 10 in mixed ones, and 10 to 25 under first past the post.
indices_loosemore_meaning: The share of seats that went to parties beyond their share of the vote: half the sum of every gap between votes and seats.
indices_loosemore_range: Under 5 in most proportional systems and 15 to 30 under first past the post.
indices_volatility_meaning: The net share of the vote that changed hands between parties since the previous election. Parties that merged or were renamed are joined across the two elections.
indices_volatility_range: Under 10 in stable party systems, 10 to 20 in a typical election, and above 30 when old parties collapse.
indices_nationalization_meaning: How evenly the parties' votes spread across the country, weighted by each party's size. A score of 1 means every party won the same share everywhere.
indices_nationalization_range: Above 0.8 where the main parties compete everywhere, and lower where regional parties are strong.
indices_caveat_pooled_independents: Independents and minor candidates reported as one group count as many small parties, not one large one.
indices_caveat_uncontested_excluded: Seats won unopposed are left out, because no votes were counted for them.
indices_caveat_first_round_votes: Votes come from the first round, and seats from the final result.
indices_caveat_list_votes: Votes are the party list votes, and seats include those won in districts.
indices_caveat_sisters_joined: Sister parties that never run against each other count as one party.
indices_caveat_alliance_seats_credited: Seats won by an alliance are credited to its member parties.
indices_caveat_alliances_as_units: Alliances count as single parties, because their votes aren't split by party.
indices_caveat_lineage_joined: Parties that merged, were renamed, or were refounded are joined to the parties they came from.
indices_caveat_split_new: Parties that split off count as new parties.
indices_caveat_unmatched_major: A large party has no recorded predecessor or successor, so its whole share counts as change.
indices_caveat_few_units: Measured over fewer than ten places, so read it loosely.

indices_rules_body:
The archive computes indices for a chamber when the chamber is filled by party and the votes behind it were counted. That means at least 10 seats, results for at least half of them, party candidates in at least half of the seats won, and at least two parties with votes. Presidents, mayors, and other single-seat races get no indices, and neither do nonpartisan bodies.

The figures use the chamber's general election as a whole. In a two-round system, votes come from the first round, when every party is on the ballot, and seats come from the final result. In a mixed system such as Germany's or Italy's, votes are the party list votes, and seats are the chamber's full membership across every tier. Under the single transferable vote, as in Ireland, votes are first preferences.
indices_effective_body:
The effective number of parties, from Markku Laakso and Rein Taagepera (1979), counts parties by weighing each one by its size: `N = 1 / Σ pᵢ²`, where `pᵢ` is a party's share of the votes or of the seats. Ten equal parties give 10; one party with 70% and three with 10% each give about 1.9. The archive reports it twice: by votes, for the electorate's choices, and by seats, for the chamber that came out of them.

Rae fragmentation, `F = 1 − Σ pᵢ²`, is the same sum read another way: the chance that two voters, or two members, picked at random belong to different parties. The API returns it beside the effective number of parties.
indices_disproportionality_body:
The Gallagher index, or least squares index, from Michael Gallagher (1991), measures how far seats stray from votes: `LSq = √(½ Σ (vᵢ − sᵢ)²)`, with vote and seat shares in percent. Squaring the gaps makes one large gap count for more than many small ones, so a winner's bonus under first past the post shows up clearly. The United Kingdom's 2024 election scored 23.7.

The Loosemore–Hanby index, `D = ½ Σ |vᵢ − sᵢ|`, adds up the gaps without squaring them. It reads as the share of seats that went to parties beyond their share of the vote. It runs higher than the Gallagher index when many small parties each fall a little short.
indices_volatility_body:
Pedersen volatility, from Mogens Pedersen (1979), measures how much of the vote changed hands since the previous election: `V = ½ Σ |pᵢ,t − pᵢ,t−1|`. The previous election is the same chamber's last general election in the archive.

A party's identity across two elections is the hard part. The archive joins two parties when its records say one merged into, succeeded, was refounded as, or was absorbed by the other, served as the other's electoral list, or is a regional branch of it. It follows the records up to four steps, and only as of the election date. A renamed party is the same party in the archive, so a new name never counts as change. A party that split off counts as a new party, so a split shows up as volatility. When a party with 10% of the vote or more has no match on the other side, the figure carries a note: the whole share counts as change, which may reflect a gap in the records more than it reflects voters moving.
indices_nationalization_body:
The party system nationalization score, from Mark Jones and Scott Mainwaring (2003), measures how evenly parties' votes spread across the country. For each party, it takes the Gini coefficient of the party's vote share across the places where votes were counted. The formula is `PNS = 1 − Gini`. The score for the whole system weighs each party's score by its share of the vote: `PSNS = Σ pᵢ × PNSᵢ`.

The archive uses it over other measures because it runs from 0 to 1, is simple to compute and explain, and is widely used. That makes it easy to compare with published work. The places are the finest level the archive reports for the chamber's counted votes, such as constituencies in the United Kingdom or states in Germany, and each counts once regardless of size. The Gini coefficient is sensitive to the number of places, so a score measured over fewer than ten carries a note.
indices_calls_body:
Each of these choices changes the numbers, so each figure lists the ones that applied to it.

- **Independents and others.** Some sources report independents or minor candidates as one group. For the effective number of parties by votes, that group counts as many tiny parties, not one large one, and each independent seat counts as its own party. The disproportionality indices treat the group as one row.
- **Alliances.** When a source reports an alliance's seats and credits them to its member parties, the archive credits them too. When an alliance's votes aren't split by party, as in Italy, the alliance counts as one party, in both elections when it measures volatility.
- **Sister parties.** Parties in a standing alliance that never run against each other, such as Germany's CDU and CSU, count as one party.
- **Uncontested seats.** Seats won unopposed have no votes, so they are left out of every figure, and the figure says how many.
- **Rounds and tiers.** First-round votes in two-round systems, list votes in mixed systems, and first preferences under the single transferable vote, as described above.
indices_access_body: Every figure comes with its inputs and notes from the API: `/api/v1/elections/{id}/indices` for each chamber an election filled, `/api/v1/contests/{id}/indices` for a list contest, and `/api/v1/polities/{id}/indices` for a country's whole series. The same data is in the MCP tools `get_election_indices`, `get_contest_indices`, and `get_polity_indices`, and in the Markdown and JSON versions of election and country pages.

accounts_lede: Contributors, most recently active first. Open an account to set limits, ban it, or revert its published work.
account_limits_none: This account has never been limited.
account_days_hint: Leave empty to keep it in place until it's lifted.
account_ban_lede: A ban signs the account out, rejects its API keys, and stops new proposals and comments. Its published work stays until you revert it.
account_revert_lede: Queue a revert for each of this account's proposals published since a date, newest first. Reverts that fail are listed below with the reason.
recent_lede: Everything that changed in the archive, newest first: data imports, proposals and their decisions, and discussion. Times are in your time zone; hover over one to see it in UTC.
recent_lede_read_only: Every data import in the archive, newest first. Times are in your time zone; hover over one to see it in UTC.
recent_in_polity: In {polity} and the places within it
proposals_lede: Corrections and additions that contributors have submitted, with the decision on each.
watchlist_lede: Changes to the records, places, proposals, and people you watch.
watchlist_empty: Watch a record, place, proposal, or contributor to see its changes here.
watchlist_quiet: Nothing new from what you watch.
watchlist_feed_lede: Add this address to a feed reader to follow your watchlist. Anyone with the address can read it, so keep it private.
watchlist_feed_rotated: New address ready. The old one no longer works.
watchlist_feed_needs_profile: Pick a handle to get a private feed of your watchlist.
history_lede: Every published change to this record, from data imports and contributors' proposals, newest first.
history_empty: No published change has touched this record yet.
history_no_fields: This change linked to the record without changing any of its fields.
history_revert_body: Reverting undoes the proposal's changes in a new changeset. The reason is public and appears on the proposal.
history_revert_queued: Revert queued. The proposal page shows its progress.
notifications_lede: Replies, mentions, and reviews of your proposals, plus activity on what you watch. Opening this page marks what it shows as read.
notifications_empty_all: Nothing yet. You'll hear here when someone replies to you, mentions you, or reviews your proposals, and when something you watch changes.
notifications_empty_direct: Nothing for you yet. Replies, mentions, and reviews of your proposals show up here.
notifications_empty_watched: Nothing from your watchlist yet. Watch a record, place, proposal, or contributor to follow it here.
notify_settings_lede: Choose which notifications also reach your inbox. Everything always appears on your notifications page.
notify_settings_direct: Email me about replies, mentions, and reviews of my proposals
notify_settings_direct_hint: Sent a few minutes after the first notification. Anything else that arrives in the meantime is added to the same email.
notify_settings_digest_hint: A summary of activity on everything you watch. Skipped when nothing happened.
notify_settings_unverified: Verify your email address to get notification email. Until then, notifications only appear on your notifications page.
unsubscribe_body_direct: You won't get email about replies, mentions, or reviews of your proposals. They'll still appear on your notifications page.
unsubscribe_body_digest: You won't get the watchlist digest anymore. Your watchlist stays as it is.
unsubscribe_done_digest: You're unsubscribed from the watchlist digest.
unsubscribe_already: You're already unsubscribed from these emails.
unsubscribe_invalid: This unsubscribe link doesn't work. It may be from an old email. Sign in to change your email settings.

match.countPlural=one: Something on Elections Archive needs your attention.
match.countPlural=*: {countText} things on Elections Archive need your attention.

notify_direct_reason: You're getting this because someone replied to you, mentioned you, or reviewed one of your proposals on Elections Archive.
notify_digest_more: Here are the latest {count}. Your watchlist has the rest.
notify_digest_reason_daily: You're getting this because you turned on the daily watchlist digest.
notify_digest_reason_weekly: You're getting this because you turned on the weekly watchlist digest.
bounties_lede: Each bounty is a gap the archive knows about: results it doesn't hold yet, with the sources already tried. Claim one, find the records, and propose them. Publishing the proposal fills the bounty and credits you.
bounties_blocked_lede: Blocked bounties have a source that a script can't reach, because it sits behind a login, a form, or a request by mail. A person can often get it in a few minutes.
bounties_footer: The list comes from the archive's register of known gaps and updates when that register changes.
bounty_sign_in: Sign in to claim this bounty
bounty_verify: Verify your email to claim this bounty
bounty_claim_hint: A claim tells others you're working on this. It lasts seven days, and you can renew it. You can propose without claiming.
bounty_held_hint: Someone else is working on this. Watch it to hear when the claim ends or the bounty is filled.
bounty_blocked_hint: A script can't reach this source. If you can get the records by hand, upload them with your proposal as evidence.
bounty_closed: Closed on {date}: the gap no longer appears in the register.
notifications_menu_empty: Nothing yet. Replies, mentions, reviews of your proposals, and changes to what you watch show up here.
livemap_description: Follow the {title} on a full-screen map of every state, House district, and county, updated as votes are counted.
livemap_legend_last: Shade shows the margin in the last election
livemap_legend_waiting_hint: Each place takes its leader's color as votes come in. Choose Last time to see the previous result.
livemap_not_here: This race isn't on the ballot here.
livemap_turnout: {share} of last time's vote counted so far
livemap_tile_nation: Explore every state and county as results come in, compared with last time.
livemap_tile_state: Explore every county as results come in, compared with last time.
board_tile_body: Pick the races you follow and watch them side by side on one screen.
live_views_label: Other ways to follow the results
livemap_counted_share: Share of the expected vote counted
livemap_near_seat_hint: Click to see this district's results
livemap_up_hint: Or click anywhere outside this area
downloads_lede: The whole archive as files you can download: every result, election, candidate, party, and boundary, in Parquet and CSV, with the sources and changes behind them. Each release is a fixed snapshot with its own version number.
downloads_empty: The first release hasn't been published. Until it is, you can read any page as Markdown or JSON, or query the archive through the API.
downloads_description: {results} results from {elections} elections in {countries} countries, {first} to {last}, with candidates, parties, and boundaries, as Parquet and CSV files. Release {version}.
downloads_description_short: Release {version} of the archive: every result, with candidates, parties, and boundaries, as Parquet and CSV files ({size}).
downloads_dataset_version_name: Elections Archive: election results worldwide, release {version}
downloads_not_latest: You're looking at an earlier release.
downloads_countries_lede: Each bar runs from a country's first election in the archive to its latest. Open a row to see its levels of government, reporting units, election types, and counting rules.
downloads_shapes_lede: Shapes for the places results are reported in, by boundary set. A place whose borders changed has one shape for each version.
downloads_files_lede: Each table comes as Parquet and as gzipped CSV, split by license bundle and, for results, by country. Boundaries are GeoParquet only. Every link below stays on this site and forwards to the file on GitHub.
downloads_sizes_caption: Download size by license bundle and format
downloads_shared_sql: DuckDB script that opens every Parquet file as a view
downloads_shared_manifest: Every file with its table, bundle, rows, size, and checksum
downloads_shared_attribution: The sources, and the credit each license asks for
downloads_geoparquet: GeoParquet: Parquet with geometry stored as WKB
downloads_quickstart_lede: Three commands take you from nothing to SQL over the whole archive. You need the GitHub CLI and DuckDB.
downloads_step_download: Download the Parquet files, the DuckDB script, and the checksums.
downloads_step_verify: Check that every file arrived intact.
downloads_step_open: Open DuckDB. Each table is ready as a view.
downloads_stable_lede: Links under /downloads/latest/ always point to the newest release, so scripts that use them keep working when a new one comes out.
downloads_licenses_lede: Files come in three bundles, one for each license. Most of the archive is CC BY 4.0. Share-alike and ODbL sources sit in bundles of their own so you can leave them out.
